scope: 20 original AQA AS Physics 7408 Waves 3.3.2.3 cards on plane refraction, step-index core/cladding, total internal reflection, dispersion and attenuation
notes: Original single-point recall, not official past paper wording; 40 valid and 40 wrong examples must be checked with actual local flashcard marker.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a step-index optical fibre, which part carries light along the fibre?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Relative to the core, what must the refractive index of an optical fibre's cladding be?
accept: smaller than the core's refractive index

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is an optical fibre's cladding useful in addition to its refractive-index difference?
cards.back: It protects the core boundary from damage and reduces light leakage.
accept: It protects the core boundary from damage and reduces light leakage.
protects core surface and reduces light loss
reject: it changes light into electrical current
it must absorb all reflected light

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a medium with speed v, express its absolute refractive index n.
accept: speed in vacuum divided by speed in material

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What approximate absolute refractive index is used for air in AS Physics calculations?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: At a plane boundary, what equation relates refractive indices n₁,n₂ and angles measured to the normal?
accept: n1 sin theta1 = n2 sin theta2

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: A wave travels from n₁ into lower n₂. What equation gives the critical angle θc?
accept: sin critical angle = lower index / higher index

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How are the incidence and refraction angles in Snell's law measured?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: At the critical angle, what angle does the refracted ray make with the normal?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When can total internal reflection occur at a boundary between two media?
cards.back: From higher n to lower n, with incidence greater than the critical angle.
accept: From higher n to lower n, with incidence greater than the critical angle.
n1 greater than n2 and i greater than critical angle
reject: from lower n to higher n
at any angle if the cladding is thick

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: During total internal reflection, how does the reflection angle compare with the angle of incidence?
accept: angle of reflection equals incidence angle

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For material dispersion, what causes different parts of a light pulse to arrive at different times?
cards.back: Different wavelengths travel at different speeds in the material.
accept: Different wavelengths travel at different speeds in the material.
different refractive indices for different wavelengths
reject: all wavelengths travel at identical speed
the detector slows all photons equally

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For modal dispersion, what makes parts of the light signal arrive at different times?
cards.back: Different ray paths have different path lengths.
accept: Different ray paths have different path lengths.
reject: all rays have the same path length
the light changes colour inside every reflection

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What effect does dispersion have on a finite-width light pulse?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can pulse broadening reduce the maximum data rate in an optical fibre?
accept: neighbouring pulses become harder to distinguish

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the main effect of absorption on signal pulses travelling along a fibre?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How is the refractive index profile modelled in a step-index fibre?
cards.back: A sharp change from core index to lower cladding index.
accept: A sharp change from core index to lower cladding index.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: If blue light has a larger refractive index than red light in the same fibre, which travels more slowly?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: If n increases, what happens to wave speed in the same kind of refractive-index comparison?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For light guided by total internal reflection, how must incidence angle compare with critical angle?
cards.back: Incidence must exceed the critical angle.
accept: Incidence must exceed the critical angle.
angle of incidence greater than critical angle
